Hi everyone,

I'm new to R and in my app i'm trying to able the user select different data frames in a "selectInput" and then change the columns (dates) in this data frame selected through a sliderInput.

Here's my code:
Ui.r
      selectInput("indicador1", label = "Escolha um indicador para exibir:",
                                                          choices = list("RCV","RIM","RCM","EAC","RFE","RAD","TCD",
                                                                         "GCA","GCP","GOC","GCI")),
                                              sliderInput("Ano","Selecione um ano para exibir:", value = 2009,
                                                          min = 2009, max = 2011, sep = "")

Server.r

datasetInput <- reactive({
  ano   <- input$Ano
  dados <- switch(input$indicador1,"RCV" = RCV[, input$Ano],"RIM" = RIM[, input$Ano],"RCM" = RCM[, input$Ano], "EAC" = EAC[, input$Ano],
           "RFE" = RFE[, input$Ano], "RAD" = RAD[, input$Ano], "TCD" = TCD[, input$Ano], "GCA" = GCA[, input$Ano], "GCP" = GCP[, input$Ano],
           "GOC" = GOC[, input$Ano], "GCI" = GCI[, input$Ano])

})

  output$chart2_3 <- renderChart2({
    n1 <- Highcharts$new()
    n1$title(text = input$indicador1)
    n1$chart(width = 980, height= 620, polar = TRUE)
    n1$data(x = c(RCV$Instituto), y = datasetInput(), type = "column", color = "#8fc74a", name = input$indicador1, label = input$indicador1)
    n1$xAxis(categories = c(RIM$Instituto))
    n1$legend(align = 'right',verticalAlign = 'middle',layout = 'vertical')
    n1$plotOptions(column = list(colorByPoint = FALSE))
    return(n1)
  })

When i put a specific value in the columns of "dados" e.g  dados <- switch(input$indicador1,"RCV" = RCV[,3],"RIM" = RIM[,3],"RCM" = RCM[,3], "EAC" = EAC[,3], "RFE" = RFE[,3], "RAD" = RAD[,3], "TCD" = TCD[,3], "GCA" = GCA[,3], "GCP" = GCP[,3],"GOC" = GOC[,3], "GCI" = GCI[,3])
  My selecInput works well, but in thi way i can't change the dates with sliderInput.

Best regards,

Filipe

Hi,
I wrote an image processing app https://piccolbo.shinyapps.io/photo-decomp/. It works locally but once deployed it fails (generic error message doesn't say anything). From reading around, I suppose it's the excessive startup time. This app computes an image decomposition at startup and it's slow, thanks to the slow-poke package EBImage (which boasts a "constant time median filter algorithm", would you believe it?"). Eventually, the image decomposition needs to move to the server code. I was wondering if you had clear guidelines as the max server startup and server update time on shinyapps. I couldn't find two clear numbers from searching around this group. Thanks

messages.body_plain:
I don't know whether this is properly a

* shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> vs. Shiny Server web hosting question,
* a `shiny` question,
* a question about browsers,
* a question about operating systems, or
* a question about the interaction between some subset of the above four domains.

So believe me I'm not expecting immediate help on this:  I just think it's an issue worth reporting.

I have an R Markdown document, with `runtime:  shiny`.   Relevant source code is in a GitHub repo <https://github.com/homerhanumat/shinyTutorials/tree/master/sim_tutorial_Rmd>.  The document calls seven related Shiny apps.  For example, here is the code chunk for the first app:

```{r, echo=FALSE}
shinyAppDir(
  "example_sim_01/",
  options=list(
    width="100%", height=550
  )
)
```

When I run the document locally, all of the apps display correctly.  (I have tried this on Ubuntu 14.04 with Firefox, and on Mac OSX Yosemite with Safari.)

I have deployed the app to shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>.  (See http://homer.shinyapp.io/sim_tutorial_Rmd).

When I am on my Linux platform, the all of the called in the deployed app display correctly.  (On Linux I have tried this only with Firefox.

On Windows 7 and on Mac OS X I find a problem, with all of the browsers I have tried so far:

* Chrome and IE on Windows 7 (no problem seen yet with Firefox);
* Safari and Firefox on Mac OSX

The "problem" is this:  for one or more of the apps (usually some subset of apps 2-5, but occasionally app 1 or app 6 as well, never app 7), the ui appears but initial output in the main panel does not appear.  If I refresh, then some of the affected apps may display correctly.

I cannot detect any pattern for which apps will be affected on initial view, nor for which apps will be corrected upon refresh.

All tested browsers are up to date.  shiny and shinyapps are up to date.

I would have access to a Shiny Server through my college.  Once some perms are set I should be able to install the app there and test for whether it's a means-of-hosting issue (shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> vs. Shiny Server).

Based on my data so far,  I'm leaning towards it being a browser-for-platform issue.

Any thoughts?

Homer

messages.subject_clean: Problems with, and best practice for, rendering images on shinyapps.io
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I'm building an application where users compare images, and I need them to be able to click on whichever image they choose. I've set this up so that there are two side-by-side actionLink buttons, and the icons are images:

output$survey <- renderUI({
        index$i
        if(max(isolate(index$i)) == length(things) && isTRUE(all.equal(things, previous_things))) {
            list(p("Finished sorting"))
        } else {
            ## but image links in the UI
            list(
              # creating a new box which spans 4
                column(width=1,
                        actionLink("goButton1", label=NULL,
                                 icon=img(src=things[index$i[1]],
                                          width = 400, height = 300))),
                column(width=1, offset=10,
                       actionLink("goButton2", label=NULL,
                           icon=img(src=things[index$i[2]],
                                    width = 400, height = 300)))
                      )
         }
    })

Locally, I've managed to successfully render the images by having the img(src=things)... be the absolute file path to the images:

things <- paste("D:\\Documents\\Research\\compactness\\img\\", things, ".jpg", sep=""), or something similar. All good so far. To deploy, I change that file path to

things <- paste("/srv/connect/apps/compactness/img/", things, ".jpg", sep=""), and I run a sanity check print(all(file.exists(things))), which prints TRUE when I check the logs on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>. However, the images appear broken!

I've also tried variants where: the images are in the same directory as ui.R and server.R; where the images are in /srv/connect/apps/compactness/www/ and rather than providing a file path, I provide the URL, for example https://arkaufman.shinyapps.io/compactness/01_0_001.jpg, which if you check that URL, will still render the image independently. I've also tried quite a few other things. I have no idea what could be so different!

I would greatly appreciate any advice here. I'm glade to provide more code if it would be helpful.

Thanks!
Aaron

1. we need to be able to connect to our server to fetch data in real time. This means we need to be able to store username/passwd information
2. download data from our server to shinyapps server
3. install R/Python libs for code dependencies

Just wondering if RStudio folks or community have addressed similar issues before.

Best,
-Abhi
